author: TEDx Talks
description:
What would you do if a malicious actor used AI to hijack your face, your voice, and your life? After surviving a harrowing five-year federal cyberstalking campaign, digital safety advocate Melissa Hutchins reveals the rapidly growing threat of AI-generated deepfakes and non-consensual imagery. In this urgent and empowering talk, she explains how this technology is weaponized against women and children, and shares a practical "three-layer shield"—from establishing a family safe word to utilizing new federal laws—to help you protect your loved ones and take back control of your digital identity. Melissa Hutchins is the founder and CEO of Certifi AI, the only female-founded, survivor-led company protecting people from malicious deepfakes, unauthorized content and digital impersonations. 

Melissa started this company after surviving a severe cyberstalking case that escalated to a federal trial, an experience that teaches us all how vulnerable we all are when technology is weaponized agai
title: How to protect your identity from AI deepfakes | Melissa Hutchins | TEDxUofW

author: TEDx Talks
description: AI could accelerate the discovery of new medicines, but how quickly will those discoveries reach patients? Drawing on his grandfather’s experience with Parkinson’s disease, Alex Epstein explores the growing gap between scientific progress and clinical development. He argues that reliable biomarkers and better trial design could help researchers evaluate treatments sooner. His call for collaboration challenges scientists, companies and regulators to bring greater urgency to the medicines patients are waiting for. Alex Epstein, PhD, is a senior computational scientist at Cellular Intelligence and head of research at Second Century Foundation. He earned his doctorate at Rockefeller University, where he used single cell genomics to investigate brain aging and caloric restriction. His work brings together experimental biology, computational methods and regenerative medicine to advance treatments for diseases associated with aging. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conferenc
title: Why new medicines take so long | Alex Epstein | TEDxBoston Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description: What does wealth actually buy when someone has cancer? Drawing on her father’s illness and her experience helping a family with extensive resources, Kat Kajderowicz explores why medical information and expert opinions can still leave patients overwhelmed. As AI makes information more accessible, she argues that the next challenge is turning knowledge into coordinated care and confident decisions. Her central idea: every patient deserves a quarterback to help navigate what comes next. Kat Kajderowicz is a neuroscientist with a PhD from MIT. Her doctoral research at the Whitehead Institute explored how cells from hibernating animals survive extreme cold, with potential applications in organ preservation and therapeutic hypothermia. A Cornell University graduate and 2023 Paul & Daisy Soros Fellow, she previously conducted research at Harvard Medical School. Her experience caring for her father during his cancer illness informs her interest in helping patients navigate complex medical dec
title: Can Money Buy a Cure for Cancer? | Kat Kajderowicz | TEDxBoston Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Social media visibility can feel like success, but what does it do to identity and self-worth? 

This talk explores algorithms, online metrics and attention, examining how the pursuit of likes, views and reach can change behaviour and distort how we see ourselves. Jsky is a British creative powerhouse whose work sits at the intersection of music, fashion, broadcasting, and cultural change. Celebrated by BBC 1Xtra and Vogue Magazine amongst others, he has built a career defined by bold firsts and meaningful impact. 

A singer, songwriter, and fashion innovator, he also fronted Channel 4’s hit body‑positivity series Naked Beach and has been recognised as one of Manchester’s leading “changemakers and unsung heroes” by the Manchester Evening News as well as a “Pioneer of Colour” by the LGBT Foundation. 

His commitment to purpose-driven work continues through high-profile campaigns, including BBC Children in Need’s thousand‑mile challenge. He champions new emerging talent as a host for BB
title: The Cost of Being Seen: Why Visibility Isn't Everything | Jsky . | TEDxNorthern Quarter

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Αναδεικνύεται η νομική και θεσμική διάσταση της κλιματικής κρίσης, η οποία ως ανθρωπογενές φαινόμενο απαιτεί συλλογική δράση και ρύθμιση της ανθρώπινης συμπεριφοράς. Αναλύεται πώς οι διεθνείς δικαστικές αποφάσεις και οι νέες διακρατικές συμμαχίες διαμορφώνουν ένα πλαίσιο υποχρεώσεων για κράτη και επιχειρήσεις στο «εδώ και τώρα». Η Καθηγήτρια Μαρία Γαβουνέλη είναι Καθηγήτρια στη Νομική Σχολή του ΕΚΠΑ, μέλος του Athens PIL και Πρόεδρος της Εθνικής Επιτροπής για τα Δικαιώματα του Ανθρώπου (2019-2022).

Με διδακτορικό (Ph.D.) στο Διεθνές Δίκαιο Περιβάλλοντος από το Πανεπιστήμιο του Cambridge (Βραβείο Paul Guggenheim) και υποτροφία Fulbright στο UC Berkeley, διαθέτει πολυετή διδακτική και ερευνητική πορεία σε κορυφαία ακαδημαϊκά ιδρύματα παγκοσμίως (Chatham House, Tulane, Utrecht κ.ά.).

Είναι Πρόεδρος του Ελληνικού Κλάδου της International Law Association (ILA) και εκ των αρχισυντακτών του Yearbook of International Environmental Law (OUP). Παράλληλα, διατηρεί ηγετικούς ρόλους σε διεθνείς
title: Η γεωπολιτική της κλιματικής κρίσης | Μαρία Γαβουνέλη | TEDxPlaka

author: TEDx Talks
description: Αναδεικνύεται ο τρόπος με τον οποίο η τέχνη και το θέατρο εμπνέουν μια υπεύθυνη στάση απέναντι στη ζωή και το περιβάλλον, με έμπνευση από τον Άντον Τσέχωφ. Αναλύεται η σημασία της προσωπικής συνέπειας, της ενσυναίσθησης και της φροντίδας για τον κόσμο που μας περιβάλλει. Μια καίρια προσέγγιση για το πώς η λογοτεχνία προσφέρει μαθήματα αυτογνωσίας και συλλογικής ευθύνης στη σύγχρονη εποχή. Ο Στρατής Πανούριος είναι ηθοποιός, σκηνοθέτης, συγγραφέας και αφηγητής audiobook, με σπουδές στο Εθνικό Θέατρο, την Εταιρία Ελλήνων Θεατρικών Συγγραφέων, το New York College Athens και το University of Greenwich. Έχει συνεργαστεί με κορυφαίους φορείς όπως το Εθνικό Θέατρο Ελλάδας, το Εθνικό Θέατρο Κίνας, τον ΘΟΚ, το Μουσείο Μπενάκη και ΔΗΠΕΘΕ. Για το καινοτόμο θεατρικό πρόγραμμα στις Φυλακές Κορυδαλλού (2016-2023) τιμήθηκε από την Ελληνική Ένωση Κριτικών Θεάτρου και Παραστατικών Τεχνών, ενώ το 2018 αναδείχθηκε «Theater Director of the Year» από το Acquisition International. Έχει εκδώσει πληθώρα βιβλ
title: Ζήσε όπως ο Τσέχωφ | Στρατής Πανούριος | TEDxPlaka

author: TEDx Talks
description: Αναδεικνύεται η σύνδεση της σπατάλης τροφίμων με την κλιματική κρίση, λόγω των εκπομπών μεθανίου και της σπατάλης πόρων. Αναλύεται πώς η πρόληψη στο νοικοκυριό και οι συνειδητές συνήθειες φροντίδας λειτουργούν ως άμεσο «φρένο» στην υπερθέρμανση του πλανήτη. Katia Lasaridi is Professor in Environmental Management and Technology at Harokopio University, Athens, Greece. She works on all aspects of waste management in the context of Circular Economy with emphasis on food waste prevention, valorization and treatment, WEEE management, and Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), where she has extensive research and consultancy experience. She has served as President of the Board of the Hellenic Recycling Agency, and in Harokopio University as member of the Governing Board, Deputy Rector, and Head of the Geography Department. She is currently member of the Scientific Committee of the Hellenic Institute of Local Authorities. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format b
title: Το Κλίμα στα Σκουπίδια | Κάτια Λαζαρίδη | TEDxPlaka

author: TEDx Talks
description: Αναδεικνύεται η ανάγκη επαναπροσδιορισμού της κλιματικής επικοινωνίας, εστιάζοντας στα λάθη του παρελθόντος, όπως η χρονική μετάθεση του προβλήματος και ο ευτελισμός του στο δημόσιο λόγο. Αναλύεται πώς η απλή, άμεση αφήγηση στο «εδώ και τώρα» μπορεί να αντιμετωπίσει τη συνωμοσιολογία και να ενεργοποιήσει τους πολίτες. Η Έλλη Παπαδοπούλου είναι Senior Consultant on Sustainability and Management Systems με 26 χρόνια εμπειρίας, κάτοχος πτυχίου Διοίκησης Επιχειρήσεων από το ΟΠΑ και πιστοποιημένη Επιθεωρήτρια Συστημάτων Διαχείρισης Ποιότητας. Εξειδικεύεται στον σχεδιασμό και την υλοποίηση Στρατηγικών Βιωσιμότητας και έργων ESG για ιδιωτικούς και δημόσιους φορείς. Παράλληλα, διαθέτει εκτεταμένη εμπειρία στον εντοπισμό χρηματοδοτήσεων και τη διαχείριση εθνικών και ευρωπαϊκών περιβαλλοντικών και κοινωνικών προγραμμάτων (Life, Horizon 2020, ERASMUS+, Interreg, EEA Grants κ.ά.). Επιπλέον, πραγματοποιεί εξειδικευμένες εκπαιδεύσεις στη Στρατηγική ESG, τις πράσινες προμήθειες και το Fundraising, ε
title: Κλιματική κρίση: Η ιστορία που είπαμε λάθος | Έλλη Παπαδοπούλου | TEDxPlaka

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Exploring how climate communication must evolve by admitting past mistakes, like fostering guilt or deflecting responsibility. Focusing on ending fossil fuels offers a clear, actionable solution that moves beyond polarization and inertia. A compelling perspective on living well without oil, turning climate challenges into opportunities for innovation. Thomas Kolster is a pioneering global voice on marketing, business and sustainability. A motivational speaker, author and impact entrepreneur, he’s been called “a climate change agent” by Forbes. He coined the term Goodvertising with his first book (Goodvertising, 2012), and in The Hero Trap (2020) introduced his methodology The Arrow to help brands create real impact by enabling personal transformation.

Kolster has spoken in more than 80 countries, advising global brands like Meta, adidas, IKEA and P&G. He is founder of the Goodvertising Agency, a columnist for The Guardian, Ad Age and Forbes, and co-hosts the podcasts Purpose Hits and
title: I Got the Climate Fight Wrong | Thomas Kolster | TEDxPlaka

author: TEDx Talks
description: Εξετάζεται ο επαναπροσδιορισμός του μάρκετινγκ στην κλιματική κρίση, με έμφαση στην ειλικρίνεια και την αυτοκριτική. Αναλύονται οι παγίδες των επιφανειακών διακηρύξεων βιωσιμότητας και πώς η δημιουργικότητα μπορεί να υπηρετήσει την πραγματική περιβαλλοντική δράση. H Μάρθα Κεσίσογλου είναι υψηλόβαθμο στέλεχος εταιρικής επικοινωνίας και μάρκετινγκ, βιωσιμότητας και ESG.  Είναι η Corporate Affairs Executive Director της Nova, μέλος της United Group του κορυφαίου παρόχου τηλεπικοινωνιών και media στη Νοτιοανατολική Ευρώπη. Η καριέρα της εκτείνεται σε πάνω από 20 έτη σε ανώτερες διευθυντικές θέσεις σε θέματα εταιρικής επικοινωνίας, μάρκετινγκ και εταιρικής υπευθυνότητας, στον τραπεζικό και τουριστικό τομέα, μεταξύ των οποίων ο Διεθνής Αερολιμένας Αθηνών, η Τράπεζα Πειραιώς, η Eurobank και ο Σύνδεσμος Ελληνικών Τουριστικών Επιχειρήσεων. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Εταιρική λογοδοσία και διαφάνεια στην επικοινωνία | Μάρθα Κεσίσογλου | TEDxPlaka

author: TEDx Talks
description: Στην ομιλία με τίτλο "Και τι να κάνω εγώ δηλαδή; Πρακτικές συμβουλές για πολίτες που θέλουν να λύσουν το πρόβλημα της κλιματικής κρίσης σήμερα" εξετάζεται το πιεστικό ερώτημα του πώς μπορεί ο καθένας μας να συμβάλει ενεργά στην αντιμετώπιση της κλιματικής κρίσης, ξεπερνώντας το αίσθημα της ατομικής αβοηθητότητας. Μέσα από πρακτικές, καθημερινές προσεγγίσεις και τεκμηριωμένα παραδείγματα, αναλύονται οι τομείς όπου η αλλαγή συνηθειών έχει το μεγαλύτερο πραγματικό αντίκτυπο. Μια καίρια τοποθέτηση για το πώς η ατομική δράση μετατρέπεται σε συλλογική δύναμη και ουσιαστική λύση στο σήμερα. Ο Θοδωρής Γεωργακόπουλος είναι δημοσιογράφος, συγγραφέας και ιδρυτής της εταιρείας ερευνών 1830 Lab. Έχει εργαστεί ως αρθρογράφος σε περιοδικά, εφημερίδες και ψηφιακά μέσα, ως μεταφραστής και επιμελητής βιβλίων, ως στέλεχος εταιρείας ΜΜΕ και ως ιδρυτικό μέλος & editorial director του ανεξάρτητου μη-κερδοσκοπικού οργανισμού διαΝΕΟσις. Από το 2013 αρθρογραφεί στην εφημερίδα Καθημερινή. Έχει γράψει πέντε βιβ
title: Και τι να κάνω εγώ δηλαδή; | Θοδωρής Γεωργακόπουλος | TEDxPlaka

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Με τίτλο ομιλίας "Ανθεκτική πόλη δεν είναι μόνο εκείνη που αντέχει στις κλιματικές αλλαγές. Είναι εκείνη που δεν αφήνει κανέναν να κινδυνεύσει αόρατος" η Αγνή Μαριακάκη εξετάζει την έννοια της κλιματικής ανθεκτικότητας μέσα από το πρίσμα της «ανθρώπινης υποδομής» και του αόρατου σώματος της πόλης, το οποίο συγκροτείται από την εμπιστοσύνη και τις κοινωνικές σχέσεις. Αναλύεται πώς η κοινωνική απομόνωση μετατρέπεται σε παράγοντα επικινδυνότητας κατά τη διάρκεια ακραίων φαινομένων, καθώς και η σημασία του κοινωνικού κεφαλαίου και της διαφορετικότητας ως δικλείδας ασφαλείας. Μια καίρια τοποθέτηση για το ότι ανθεκτική πόλη δεν είναι απλώς εκείνη που διαθέτει τεχνικές υποδομές, αλλά εκείνη όπου κανείς δεν κινδυνεύει αόρατος και αφημένος. Διευθύντρια της MindSearch από το 1995

Εξειδίκευση στην εξωλεκτική επικοινωνία

Διαπιστευμένη στη διαχείριση τραυματος 

Συγγραφέας δ
title: Ανθεκτική πόλη είναι εκείνη που δεν αφήνει κανέναν αόρατο στην κρίση | Αγνή Μαριακάκη | TEDxPlaka

author: TEDx Talks
description: Alors que la crise du logement s’aggrave et que le bâtiment manque de main-d’œuvre, nous devons apprendre à construire plus rapidement sans sacrifier la qualité, la solidité ni la beauté. L’impression 3D appliquée à la construction permet déjà de réaliser les murs de bâtiments en quelques heures, y compris dans des territoires difficiles d’accès. Cette technologie n’est ni une solution miracle ni une invitation à construire toujours davantage, mais un outil complémentaire pour répondre à des besoins urgents. Le futur de la construction n’est plus de la science-fiction : il est déjà à l’œuvre, ici sur Terre. Manon Borloo travaille dans le développement international de technologies appliquées à la construction. Après plusieurs années dans le secteur de l’énergie, en France et aux États-Unis, elle rejoint Constructions-3D, une entreprise française spécialisée dans l’impression 3D appliquée au bâtiment. Elle accompagne aujourd’hui le déploiement de cette technologie à l’international et
title: Imprimer le monde qui vient | Manon Borloo | TEDxLeboncoin

author: TEDx Talks
description:
À rebours d’un discours ambiant fondé sur la peur et la méfiance, Emmanuel Arnaud défend une conviction simple : l’immense majorité des gens sont bien intentionnés et dignes de confiance. L’échange de maisons en apporte une preuve concrète en permettant à des inconnus de se confier ce qu’ils ont de plus intime et de plus précieux. Lorsqu’on retire l’argent de la relation, davantage d’attention, de tolérance et d’empathie peuvent émerger. Habiter le monde qui vient, c’est peut-être faire le choix conscient de l’habiter davantage ensemble. Diplômé de HEC Paris et de la Harvard Kennedy School, a fondé GuesttoGuest en 2011. Six ans plus tard, il rachète, aux côtés de son associé Charles-Edouard Girard, la société américaine HomeExchange, aujourd’hui plateforme n°1 de l’échange de maisons dans le monde.
Doté d’une expertise en gestion, en entrepreneuriat, dans le domaine des start-ups et en leadership, Emmanuel Arnaud est un acteur de premier plan de l’économie collaborative. Il intervient
title: Le pari de la confiance | Emmanuel Arnaud | TEDxLeboncoin

author: TEDx Talks
description: Atteindre une autre planète, y survivre et véritablement l’habiter sont trois défis très différents. Pour vivre ailleurs, nous devrions soit recréer artificiellement les conditions terrestres, soit transformer profondément les êtres humains afin qu’ils s’adaptent à leur nouveau monde. Car nous ne sommes pas simplement installés sur Terre : nos corps, nos perceptions et notre manière d’exister ont été façonnés par elle. Une humanité devenue multiplanétaire ne serait donc peut-être plus une seule humanité, mais plusieurs humanités progressivement transformées par les planètes qu’elles pensaient coloniser. Né en 1958, Etienne Klein est physicien et directeur du laboratoire de recherche sur les sciences de la matière du CEA. Également membre de l'Académie des technologies, il est l'auteur de plusieurs ouvrages dont les thématiques sont à la croisée de la physique et de la philosophie et vient de publier le livre  «Éloges du dépassement», coécrit avec Thomas Pesquet. This talk was given at
title: Notre humanité ira-t-elle se faire voir ailleurs ? | Etienne Klein | TEDxLeboncoin

author: TEDx Talks
description: Maria Fernanda Martinez-Donaus, founder of RioProgress, tells the stories of three Rio Grande Valley students who did everything right and still hit a wall: missed deadlines no one explained, financial aid offices that passed them from desk to desk, and the quiet work of becoming your own translator, researcher, and advocate just to access help you’d already been awarded. She argues the question we keep asking is backwards. It isn’t whether students are ready for college. It’s whether the systems around them are ready for students. By the end, one of these stories turns out to be closer to home than it first appears. This talk blends personal storytelling and firsthand experience working alongside students and culminates in a set of concrete recommendations for schools, colleges, and families. Maria Fernanda Martinez-Donaus is a Brownsville, Texas, native, educator, and nonprofit leader dedicated to expanding educational opportunity in the Rio Grande Valley. As the founder and executi
title: What Our Systems Ask Youth to Carry Alone | Dr. Maria Fernanda Martinez-Donaus | TEDxBrownsville

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Every small city tells its brightest kids the same thing: work hard, get your degree, and get out. This talk pushes back on that advice, arguing that what economists call brain drain carries a cost beyond the balance sheet. A community that keeps exporting its most talented people slowly loses the people who would have rebuilt it.

Using Brownsville, Texas as a case study, the talk argues that nobody is coming to fix brain drain for us, and that the most sustainable economic stimulus a hometown can get is its own people reinvesting in it: opening a coffee shop, hiring a local contractor, treating a vacant storefront as a blank canvas instead of a sign of decay. The payoff isn’t only financial, it’s a generation that no longer has to leave to chase a good life.

This talk draws on local economic data and ends with a call to action for anyone who has ever felt torn between loving their hometown and being told to leave it. A proud Brownsville native, Nalleli Trejo is a dedicated public s
title: If You Love Your Hometown, Your Hometown Will Love You Back | Nalleli Trejo | TEDxBrownsville

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the thing people call you weird for today becomes exactly what makes you valuable tomorrow?

Jocelyn Lui started making YouTube videos at eight years old and kept posting through her teenage years, even as cousins blasted her videos in the car to embarrass her and a close friend went through something similar at school. Years later, she watched those same people start posting content of their own once doing so became normal, even profitable. She traces that shift and makes the case for creating before the world decides it’s acceptable, not after.

This is a personal, coming-of-age style talk about creativity, early online culture, and the cost of waiting for permission. Raised between Mexico and the United States in a family of musicians and artists, Jocelyn Lui is a social media manager for JZD and a content creator who has spent more than a decade telling stories online. She earned a bachelor's degree in Communication Studies from The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley an
title: The courage to create before the world gives you permission | Jocelyn Lui | TEDxBrownsville

author: TEDx Talks
description:
When Leah opened her personal injury law firm, she marketed to everyone. When she narrowed her focus instead, speaking directly to women, then specifically to Latinas like her, her client base didn’t shrink. It grew, carried by people who had never heard of her but trusted someone who had. Drawing on research into trust transfer and the social dynamics of Latino consumer decisions, she introduces the idea of the “Trust Holder”: the person whose word moves an entire network before a single sale happens.

This talk blends a personal business story with cited research and lands on a practical reframe for how companies think about marketing and growth. Leah Wise was born and raised in Primera, Texas and graduated from Harlingen High School in 2008.  Upon graduation from high school, Leah attended The University of Texas at Austin where she graduated in 2012 with a Bachelor of Science in Political Communication and a concentration in women's and gender studies. Leah obtained her Doctor of
title: Why the person who buys is not always the person who matters most | Leah Wise | TEDxBrownsville

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Avoid burnout by finding a maker space in which to grow, design, and thrive. You're a master of your craft. A successful professional who knows how to execute. But there's a part of you that remembers creating for the joy of it—and you miss it. You feel the tension between "The Strategist" and "The Studio." My work is dedicated to building a bridge between those two worlds.

My name is Dr. Abigail Joseph, and I am the Architect of Joyful Results. After a 7-year PhD path in computer science and 15 years in K-12 schools, I took a "teacher gap year" to escape burnout, finding sanctuary in a makerspace. There, I rediscovered the joy I first felt as a kid making duct-taped storybooks. I remembered my creativity wasn't a distraction; it was my greatest asset.

As an innovation strategist and 2x TEDx speaker, I've dedicated my career to fusing the rigor of The Lab with the soul of The Studio, helping brilliant minds like yours build a structured process to bring your best ideas to life. This
title: Burnout is a Design Problem | Abigail Joseph | TEDxDesign Tech HS

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What do you call it when you fall completely for someone, and there was never an affair to confess?

Giana thought she’d have to come clean about infidelity. What she actually had to explain to her husband was harder to name: an involuntary, one-sided romantic obsession psychologists call limerence. She walks through what it did to her body and mind, the withdrawal, the attachment wound underneath it, and the years of work it took to get free of it, and arrives at an answer that has less to do with the other person than she expected. Giana Gallardo Hesterberg was born and raised in Brownsville, Texas. She studied at Central College in Pella, Iowa, and received a bachelor's degree in elementary education. She graduated with a master's degree in clinical mental health counseling from the University of Texas Rio Grande Valley in May of 2025. During her graduate school career, she heavily researched limerence and has presented her findings at counseling conferences. Hesterberg is a child
title: Love Lies On the Border | Giana Hesterberg | TEDxBrownsville

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Brownsville is in the middle of a historic wave of economic investment and growth. Can it change without losing what makes it home?

Marco Moreno left Brownsville to join the Army, and returning years later, he found a city transforming faster than he expected. Drawing on memories of downtown life, Charro Days, and family gatherings, he challenges the idea that communities have to choose between growth at all costs and resisting development altogether. He makes the case for a third way: one where economic opportunity and environmental stewardship, innovation and cultural identity, aren’t competing goals but can grow together.

This talk blends personal reflection (leaving home, coming back to a changed city) with a civic argument about what responsible growth actually requires. Marco Moreno is an organizational development consultant, counselor, and communication educator whose work focuses on leadership, organizational change, and human development. He partners with leaders and organ
title: Can a City Change Without Losing Itself? | Marco Moreno | TEDxBrownsville

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What happens after someone trusts you with their story? Paulina Sosa, completing her doctoral training in public health and informatics, noticed a pattern across years of interviews: we have no shortage of stories, our feeds are full of them, but we often stop paying attention the moment the camera turns off.

Sosa argues the real problem isn’t a shortage of storytelling, it’s a habit of stopping too soon. Drawing on interviews that range from a family-owned brewery that became a community lifeline during the pandemic to patterns she noticed in caregiving stories, she introduces what she calls story stewardship: a five-part practice for staying responsible to a story once someone has entrusted it to you. Her case is that the question we ask after “how do we share this” should be “what is this story asking us to notice.”

This talk includes personal interviews and a practical framework for listening, built for anyone who works with other people’s stories: in public health, education, b
title: We’ve Been Using Storytelling Wrong – How to fix it | Dr. Paulina Sosa-Quintanilla | TEDxBrownsville

description:
Why do we call the same skill “entrepreneurship” on a stage and just “getting by” at the flea market? Daniel Pizana grew up working the pulga, doing janitor work, and selling door to door in Brownsville, and he noticed that the skills his community uses every day, reading demand, managing trust, solving problems with no room for error, are the same skills taught in business school, just without the vocabulary to name them.

In this talk, Pizana makes the case for what he calls self-power: the refusal to hand over authority over your own life just because greatness has never been named inside your community. Drawing on his own path from the flea market to law and startups, he argues that the real barrier most people face isn’t talent or opportunity, it’s permission, and he challenges viewers to stop waiting for someone else to call them ready.

This talk includes a personal story and is aimed at anyone who has ever underestimated their own experience. Daniel Pizana is a Brownsville att
title: Why everyday work is already genius | Daniel Pizana | TEDxBrownsville

author: TEDx Talks
description:
For almost twenty years, Ester has raised a family of ten in two beds inside a self-built home in a Rio Grande Valley colonia, with no paved road to it and, until recently, no secure legal claim to the land underneath her. She’s one of nearly 200,000 people living across the Valley’s 1,200 colonias, part of a pattern repeated in roughly 2,400 similar settlements along the entire U.S. border.

Andrik Gonzalez argues that colonias didn’t happen by accident. They grew out of a regulatory gap between what developers were allowed to sell and what local government was required to provide, a gap that decades of housing funding have barely touched. Drawing on income, employment, and education data from across the Valley, he makes the case that neglect became infrastructure, built one policy decision at a time, and asks what it will take for the region’s coming growth to finally include the people already here.

This talk includes a personal story and regional data on poverty, housing, and pub
title: The Valley Is Growing and Not Everyone Is Growing With It | Andrik Gonzalez | TEDxBrownsville

description: Every time we tap a button, make a payment, or open an app, technology makes a series of decisions behind the scenes. Most of the time, we never notice them. We simply expect everything to work. In this talk, Raghvendra Kamarthi explores how automation is changing the way we build and use technology. Drawing from his experience in cloud computing, platform engineering, and infrastructure automation, he explains why making systems faster and more efficient is only part of the challenge. Through a real-world example of an automated system repeatedly trying to fix the same problem, Raghvendra highlights an important lesson: automation can reduce human error, but it can also repeat mistakes at a scale and speed that people cannot easily control. As AI systems become increasingly capable of making decisions and taking action, he invites us to think beyond what technology can do and consider what it should do, where human judgment is needed, and who remains accountable for the outcome. title: What Should We Let Technology Decide for Us? | Raghvendra Kamarthi | TEDxCNS Pune Youth
